Article 33

1. In providing protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children, the Regional Government may cooperate with the Government, Provincial Government, other Regency/City Governments and other institutions. (2) Cooperation between the Regional Government and the Provincial Government or the Government includes consultation, coordination, advocacy, referral, monitoring, evaluation and reporting.
3. Cooperation between the Regional Government and Regency/City includes coordination, advocacy and referral.
4. The implementation of cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) is in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Banyumas Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Banyumas.
4. Regional Apparatus Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is a regional apparatus assigned with specific principal duties and authorities in the region.
5. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
6. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, as well as receive protection from violence and discrimination.
8. Protection Implementation is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and services for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Violence Against Children.
9. Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment carried out on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing, eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
10. Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment carried out against children, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.
11. Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who, because of their gender, experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
12. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment whether physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
13. Victim Recovery is all efforts to empower victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually.
14. Companion is a social worker who has professional competence in their field.
15. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the purpose of empowering victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face.
16. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing victims and communities that support the reunification of victims into a family environment or family substitute that can provide protection and fulfillment of the victim's needs.
17. Safe House is a temporary residence used to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children in accordance with determined operational standards.
18. Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Violence Against Children, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT PKBGA, is a special service place for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children carried out cross-functionally and cross-sectorally as one unit of implementation so that victims receive maximum service in an integrated and comprehensive manner.
19. Sub-District Level Complaint Service Institution, hereinafter abbreviated as LPPTK, is a special service place for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children located at the sub-district level so that victims receive maximum service in an integrated and comprehensive manner.

Article 11

Other violence as referred to in Article 5 letter f is caused by:

a. threats of violence include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and
b. coercion includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

NUMBER 3 OF 2015

CONCERNING

THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION 'FBRHABAP KOREAN

GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

The right to a decent life, dignity and honor of women and children should properly receive protection in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination and the possibility of acts of violence.

The policy of protection services for victims of gender-based violence and children has been normatively regulated in the Regulation of the State Minister for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of the Republic of Indonesia Number 01 of 2010 concerning Minimum Service Standards in the field of Integrated Services for women and children victims of violence.

Concrete steps that can be taken by the Regional Government so that women and children are protected from acts of violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, can be done by implementing a legal rule embodied in the form of a regional regulation. - The formulation of norms regarding the protection of women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations needs to be carried out, the enactment of regional regulations is in order to reinforce institutional support.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims of violence, especially in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence, community participation, implementation mechanisms, guidance, funding as well as guidance and supervision.

CHAPTER VI

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 34

1. Guidance and Supervision of the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children is carried out by the Regent.
2. The implementation of guidance and supervision of the provision of protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by the SKPD responsible for women's empowerment and child protection.

Article 17

Prevention efforts as referred to in Article 16 letter a include:

a. conducting communication, information, and education about gender-based and child violence;

b. disseminating laws and regulations related to gender-based and child violence.

Article 2

Point a What is meant by "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims of gender-based violence and children without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status and physical or mental condition.

Point b What is meant by "best interests of the victim" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, and the judiciary, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

Point c What is meant by "gender justice" is fair treatment given to women and men.

What is meant by "gender equality" is a condition and position that describes a harmonious, balanced relationship between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances in access, participation, control and benefits in the implementation of development and enjoying the results of development in family life, as well as in society, nation and state.

Point d What is meant by "victim protection" is providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions.

Point e What is meant by "maternal survival" is ensuring that a mother does not experience death that occurs during pregnancy, childbirth, and postpartum, whether caused by physical or non-physical conditions.

Point f What is meant by "growth and development" of children is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to education, the right to play, the right to create and recreate.

What is meant by "survival" of children is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to identity and the right to enjoy the highest attainable health status.

Point g What is meant by "respect for the views of the child" is respect for children's rights to participate and express their opinions in decision-making, especially if it concerns matters that affect their lives.

Point h What is meant by "transparency" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is transparent among service providers.

Point i What is meant by "integration" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is carried out by building coordination among service providers, including medical services, legal assistance, psychologists, clergy, social workers, police.

Point j What is meant by "not blaming the victim" is an attitude and treatment of not blaming the victim for the occurrence of violence experienced.

Point k What is meant by "empowerment" is that every effort given must be able to strengthen the victim, both physically, psychologically, socially and economically.

Point l What is meant by "victim confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure the victim is in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of the victim.

Point m What is meant by "decision-making in the hands of the victim" is the victim's right to determine the best choice in resolving their problem.

Article 4

The scope of protection for Victims includes prevention, service and empowerment efforts for victims of violence.

Article 25

Monitoring and reporting as referred to in Article 16 letter i. includes monitoring, documentation and reporting of cases of gender-based violence and violence against children.

CHAPTER IX

TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

Article 37

At the time this Regional Regulation comes into force, all regional legal products related to the protection of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children are declared to remain in force as long as they do not conflict with and/or have not been replaced by new regulations.

CHAPTER IX

TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

Article 37

At the time this Regional Regulation comes into force, all regional legal products ^ related to the protection of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children are declared to remain in force as long as they do not conflict with and/or have not been replaced by new regulations.

Article 14

In implementing protection for victims of gender-based and child violence, the Regional Government is assisted by:

a. PPT PKBGA; and
b. LPPTK.T 10

Article 30

In carrying out the duties as referred to in Article 29, LPPTK is obliged to:
a. coordinate and consult with PPT PKBGA; b. document and report every case of gender-based violence and violence against children handled to PPT PKBGA.

NUMBER 3 OF 2015

CONCERNING

THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION 'FBRHABAP KOREAN

GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

The right to a decent life, dignity and honor of women and children should properly receive protection in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination and the possibility of acts of violence.

The policy of protection services for victims of gender-based violence and children has been normatively regulated in the Regulation of the State Minister for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of the Republic of Indonesia Number 01 of 2010 concerning Minimum Service Standards in the field of Integrated Services for women and children victims of violence.

Concrete steps that can be taken by the Regional Government so that women and children are protected from acts of violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, can be done by implementing a legal rule embodied in the form of a regional regulation. - The formulation of norms regarding the protection of women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations needs to be carried out, the enactment of regional regulations is in order to reinforce institutional support.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims of violence, especially in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence, community participation, implementation mechanisms, guidance, funding as well as guidance and supervision.

Article 2

Point a What is meant by "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims of gender-based violence and children without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status and physical or mental condition.

Point b What is meant by "best interests of the victim" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, and the judiciary, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

Point c What is meant by "gender justice" is fair treatment given to women and men.

What is meant by "gender equality" is a condition and position that describes a harmonious, balanced relationship between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances in access, participation, control and benefits in the implementation of development and enjoying the results of development in family life, as well as in society, nation and state.

Point d What is meant by "victim protection" is providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions.

Point e What is meant by "maternal survival" is ensuring that a mother does not experience death that occurs during pregnancy, childbirth, and postpartum, whether caused by physical or non-physical conditions.

Point f What is meant by "growth and development" of children is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to education, the right to play, the right to create and recreate.

What is meant by "survival" of children is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to identity and the right to enjoy the highest attainable health status.

Point g What is meant by "respect for the views of the child" is respect for children's rights to participate and express their opinions in decision-making, especially if it concerns matters that affect their lives.

Point h What is meant by "transparency" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is transparent among service providers.

Point i What is meant by "integration" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is carried out by building coordination among service providers, including medical services, legal assistance, psychologists, clergy, social workers, police.

Point j What is meant by "not blaming the victim" is an attitude and treatment of not blaming the victim for the occurrence of violence experienced.

Point k What is meant by "empowerment" is that every effort given must be able to strengthen the victim, both physically, psychologically, socially and economically.

Point l What is meant by "victim confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure the victim is in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of the victim.

Point m What is meant by "decision-making in the hands of the victim" is the victim's right to determine the best choice in resolving their problem.

Article 4

The scope of protection for Victims includes prevention, service and empowerment efforts for victims of violence.

Article 35

Funding for protection activities for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children carried out by the Regional Government - is charged to the APBD and/or other lawful sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 14

a. PPT PKBGA; and
b. LPPTK.T 10

Article 17

Prevention efforts as referred to in Article 16 letter a include:

a. conducting communication, information, and education about gender-based and child violence;

b. disseminating laws and regulations related to gender-based and child violence.

I. GENERAL

The right to a decent life, dignity and honor of women and children should properly receive protection in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination and the possibility of acts of violence.

The policy of protection services for victims of gender-based violence and children has been normatively regulated in the Regulation of the State Minister for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of the Republic of Indonesia Number 01 of 2010 concerning Minimum Service Standards in the field of Integrated Services for women and children victims of violence.

Concrete steps that can be taken by the Regional Government so that women and children are protected from acts of violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, can be done by implementing a legal rule embodied in the form of a regional regulation. - The formulation of norms regarding the protection of women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations needs to be carried out, the enactment of regional regulations is in order to reinforce institutional support.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims of violence, especially in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence, community participation, implementation mechanisms, guidance, funding as well as guidance and supervision.

What is meant by "survival" of children is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to identity and the right to enjoy the highest attainable health status.

Point l What is meant by "victim confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure the victim is in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of the victim.

GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

The right to a decent life, dignity and honor of women and children should properly receive protection in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination and the possibility of acts of violence.

The policy of protection services for victims of gender-based violence and children has been normatively regulated in the Regulation of the State Minister for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of the Republic of Indonesia Number 01 of 2010 concerning Minimum Service Standards in the field of Integrated Services for women and children victims of violence.

Concrete steps that can be taken by the Regional Government so that women and children are protected from acts of violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, can be done by implementing a legal rule embodied in the form of a regional regulation. - The formulation of norms regarding the protection of women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations needs to be carried out, the enactment of regional regulations is in order to reinforce institutional support.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims of violence, especially in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence, community participation, implementation mechanisms, guidance, funding as well as guidance and supervision.

Article 4

The scope of protection for Victims includes prevention, service and empowerment efforts for victims of violence.

Paragraph 2

Article 11

Other violence as referred to in Article 5 letter f is caused by:

a. threats of violence include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and
b. coercion includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 2

Point a What is meant by "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims of gender-based violence and children without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status and physical or mental condition.

Point b What is meant by "best interests of the victim" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, and the judiciary, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

Point c What is meant by "gender justice" is fair treatment given to women and men.

What is meant by "gender equality" is a condition and position that describes a harmonious, balanced relationship between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances in access, participation, control and benefits in the implementation of development and enjoying the results of development in family life, as well as in society, nation and state.

Point d What is meant by "victim protection" is providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions.

Point e What is meant by "maternal survival" is ensuring that a mother does not experience death that occurs during pregnancy, childbirth, and postpartum, whether caused by physical or non-physical conditions.

Point f What is meant by "growth and development" of children is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to education, the right to play, the right to create and recreate.

What is meant by "survival" of children is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to identity and the right to enjoy the highest attainable health status.

Point g What is meant by "respect for the views of the child" is respect for children's rights to participate and express their opinions in decision-making, especially if it concerns matters that affect their lives.

Point h What is meant by "transparency" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is transparent among service providers.

Point i What is meant by "integration" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is carried out by building coordination among service providers, including medical services, legal assistance, psychologists, clergy, social workers, police.

Point j What is meant by "not blaming the victim" is an attitude and treatment of not blaming the victim for the occurrence of violence experienced.

Point k What is meant by "empowerment" is that every effort given must be able to strengthen the victim, both physically, psychologically, socially and economically.

Point l What is meant by "victim confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure the victim is in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of the victim.

Point m What is meant by "decision-making in the hands of the victim" is the victim's right to determine the best choice in resolving their problem.

GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

The right to a decent life, dignity and honor of women and children should properly receive protection in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination and the possibility of acts of violence.

The policy of protection services for victims of gender-based violence and children has been normatively regulated in the Regulation of the State Minister for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of the Republic of Indonesia Number 01 of 2010 concerning Minimum Service Standards in the field of Integrated Services for women and children victims of violence.

Concrete steps that can be taken by the Regional Government so that women and children are protected from acts of violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, can be done by implementing a legal rule embodied in the form of a regional regulation. - The formulation of norms regarding the protection of women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations needs to be carried out, the enactment of regional regulations is in order to reinforce institutional support.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims of violence, especially in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence, community participation, implementation mechanisms, guidance, funding as well as guidance and supervision.

GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

The right to a decent life, dignity and honor of women and children should properly receive protection in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination and the possibility of acts of violence.

The policy of protection services for victims of gender-based violence and children has been normatively regulated in the Regulation of the State Minister for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of the Republic of Indonesia Number 01 of 2010 concerning Minimum Service Standards in the field of Integrated Services for women and children victims of violence.

Concrete steps that can be taken by the Regional Government so that women and children are protected from acts of violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, can be done by implementing a legal rule embodied in the form of a regional regulation. - The formulation of norms regarding the protection of women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations needs to be carried out, the enactment of regional regulations is in order to reinforce institutional support.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims of violence, especially in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence, community participation, implementation mechanisms, guidance, funding as well as guidance and supervision.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Banyumas Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Banyumas.
4. Regional Apparatus Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is a regional apparatus assigned with specific principal duties and authorities in the region.
5. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
6. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, as well as receive protection from violence and discrimination.
8. Protection Implementation is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and services for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Violence Against Children.
9. Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment carried out on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing, eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
10. Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment carried out against children, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.
11. Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who, because of their gender, experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
12. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment whether physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
13. Victim Recovery is all efforts to empower victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually.
14. Companion is a social worker who has professional competence in their field.
15. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the purpose of empowering victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face.
16. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing victims and communities that support the reunification of victims into a family environment or family substitute that can provide protection and fulfillment of the victim's needs.
17. Safe House is a temporary residence used to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children in accordance with determined operational standards.
18. Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Violence Against Children, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT PKBGA, is a special service place for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children carried out cross-functionally and cross-sectorally as one unit of implementation so that victims receive maximum service in an integrated and comprehensive manner.
19. Sub-District Level Complaint Service Institution, hereinafter abbreviated as LPPTK, is a special service place for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children located at the sub-district level so that victims receive maximum service in an integrated and comprehensive manner.

In providing protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children, the Regional Government may cooperate with the Government, Provincial Government, other Regency/City Governments and other institutions. 3. Cooperation between the Regional Government and Regency/City includes coordination, advocacy and referral.

The scope of protection for Victims includes prevention, service and empowerment efforts for victims of violence.

Article 25

Monitoring and reporting as referred to in Article 16 letter i. includes monitoring, documentation and reporting of cases of gender-based violence and violence against children.

In implementing protection for victims of gender-based and child violence, the Regional Government is assisted by:

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

5. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
6. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, as well as receive protection from violence and discrimination.
8. Protection Implementation is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and services for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Violence Against Children.
9. Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment carried out on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing, eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
10. Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment carried out against children, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.
11. Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who, because of their gender, experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
12. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment whether physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
13. Victim Recovery is all efforts to empower victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually.
14. Companion is a social worker who has professional competence in their field.
15. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the purpose of empowering victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face.
16. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing victims and communities that support the reunification of victims into a family environment or family substitute that can provide protection and fulfillment of the victim's needs.
17. Safe House is a temporary residence used to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children in accordance with determined operational standards.
18. Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Violence Against Children, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT PKBGA, is a special service place for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children carried out cross-functionally and cross-sectorally as one unit of implementation so that victims receive maximum service in an integrated and comprehensive manner.
19. Sub-District Level Complaint Service Institution, hereinafter abbreviated as LPPTK, is a special service place for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children located at the sub-district level so that victims receive maximum service in an integrated and comprehensive manner.

Point a What is meant by "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims of gender-based violence and children without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status and physical or mental condition.

Point c What is meant by "gender justice" is fair treatment given to women and men.

What is meant by "gender equality" is a condition and position that describes a harmonious, balanced relationship between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances in access, participation, control and benefits in the implementation of development and enjoying the results of development in family life, as well as in society, nation and state.

What is meant by "survival" of children is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to identity and the right to enjoy the highest attainable health status.

Point g What is meant by "respect for the views of the child" is respect for children's rights to participate and express their opinions in decision-making, especially if it concerns matters that affect their lives.
